title: Binding SnO2 Nanocrystals in Nitrogen-Doped Graphene Sheets as Anode Materials for Lithium-Ion Batteries

nodes.label: Lithium-ion anodes need far more capacity than graphite; SnO2 offers it but pulverises and its Sn aggregates on cycling
Binding small SnO2 nanocrystals inside nitrogen-doped graphene sheets should keep them active, intact and unaggregated
SnO2 nanocrystals as the active phase for their high theoretical lithium capacity
Nitrogen-doped reduced graphene oxide as the conducting host that binds the nanocrystals

attrs.role: electron path, volume buffer, Sn-N binding sites

nodes.label: In situ hydrazine monohydrate vapour reduction rather than a solution route, to reduce and N-dope without moving the nanocrystals

attrs.reason: keeps nanocrystal size and placement; reduces GO and dopes N in one step

nodes.label: Hydrothermal synthesis of SnO2 nanocrystals
Mix the nanocrystals into a graphene-oxide suspension and freeze-dry to a sheet-like powder
Hydrazine monohydrate vapour at 120 C for 2 h reduces the GO and dopes it with nitrogen
Current density stepped 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20 A/g and back, plus 500 cycles at fixed rate
Galvanostatic lithiation/delithiation of the electrode for 500 cycles
SnO2 nanocrystals are 4-5 nm and the vapour reduction does not coarsen them
Nanocrystals are uniformly confined inside the graphene sheets, with only a few exposed at the outer surface
The nanocrystals are polycrystalline tetragonal rutile SnO2 (JCPDS 41-1445)
Interfacial Sn-N and Sn-O-C bonds tie the nanocrystals to the doped graphene
Micropores and small mesopores (below ~5 nm) run between the sheets and the nanocrystals
Graphene carries electrons in and micropores carry Li+ in, while the sheets buffer the volume change and Sn-N bonds stop Sn coarsening
Reversible capacity is 1346 mA h/g after 500 cycles at near-100% Coulombic efficiency
Capacity falls only from ~1150 to ~420 mA h/g as the rate rises 40-fold, and recovers on return to 0.5 A/g
After 500 cycles Sn is still spread through the carbon with no Sn-rich clusters
The hybrid works as a high-rate, long-life lithium-ion anode

attrs.condition: half cell vs Li metal, 500 cycles

nodes.label: Binding SnO2 nanocrystals in nitrogen-doped graphene gives a stable, high-capacity, high-rate anode
Nitrogen is present at a few atomic percent, and Sn content climbs from the surface into the interior
C K-edge intensity at ca. 285 and 288 eV reports carbon bonded to nitrogen and oxygen species
JCPDS 41-1445: tetragonal rutile SnO2, P42/mnm, a = 4.738 A, c = 3.187 A
Capacity is not steady: it fades to ~1000 mA h/g by cycle 20 and then climbs ~35% to cycle 500
SEM at two magnifications: crumpled sheet stacks whose surfaces are smooth, with almost no nanocrystals standing proud

notes: Lost: TGA loading, EIS, and the SnO2-only and N-RGO-only control electrodes, which the packet never shows. Three audits: the C K-edge traces coincide at 285 eV where the text claims an obvious increase (o7); the first cycle loses ~36% irreversibly (o10); and the EDX O:Sn ratio rises 0.87 to 1.31 after cycling, which the text does not mention (o15). Packet defect: in the Figure 4 panel section the 'definition' strings are shifted one panel late (F4a is given the EDX caption but is the STEM image, F4b is given 'and carbon' but is the EDX spectrum, and so on), and F4i is flagged as an OCR/detector disagreement. The SAED in F1c is an unlisted inset, so o4 carries empty panel_ids.

changes: o14 panel_ids: added #F4d and #F4i. The node claims C-K, O-K and Sn-L maps before and after cycling, but the O-K panels were not cited (the packet's shifted 'definition' strings make d/i look like tin maps; their image_labels read O-K).

o13 -> n19 rel evidences -> qualifies. o13 reads that the cycled aggregate is brighter, denser and larger; that does not support 'Sn still spread with no Sn-rich clusters' (o14 does), it bounds it. n19 keeps its evidence from o14.

o1 -> n12 mm_op register_colocated_views -> inspect_local_feature. F1a (10 um) and F1b (100 nm) are not registered to a marked region; the claim 'no nanocrystals standing proud' is a judgement on the single high-magnification view, with representativeness assumed.

panel_checks.note: F2f is the C K-edge XANES with N-RGO (solid) and SnO2NC@N-RGO (dash-dot). The two traces are indistinguishable at the 285.4 eV peak and separate only above ~288 eV, clearly at 292 eV - exactly the audit the node states against the text's 'obvious increase at ca. 285 eV'.

F4a is the pristine STEM (100 nm bar, speckled sheet with a boxed region) and F4f the cycled STEM (300 nm bar, one bright dense aggregate with a boxed region). Both are the panels the node reads, and the different bars justify image_support=partial. The packet's 'definition' for F4a says 'EDX spectrum', which is wrong (see below).

F4c is the pristine C-K map, F4e the pristine Sn-L map, F4h the cycled C-K map and F4j the cycled Sn-L map; all four show the even speckle the node reads, and F4j is grainier at the particle edge but not clustered. The cited ids are all correct; the O-K maps (F4d, F4i) the node also claims were missing and have been added.

review.audit_summary: Four audits, all fair and all correctly separated by kind. o7 is a genuine figure-against-text conflict stated as a qualification rather than a contradiction, which is right: the panel shows coincidence at 285 eV, not the opposite of the bonding claim, so n14 keeps basis=argued and its other support. o10 (first-cycle efficiency ~64%) and n25 (capacity dips to ~1000 by cycle 20 then climbs) bound the capacity claim. o15 is a true text_silent finding - the O:Sn intensity ratio printed on the panels rises 0.87 to 1.31 and the text never mentions it - and it now sits with o13 on qualifies edges into n19.
